Rules / Correctness

SK2100 [ThreadStatic] is applied where it cannot take effect

A field marked [ThreadStatic] is either not static, in which case the attribute does nothing at all, or is static with an initializer, in which case only the first thread to touch the type sees the initialized value.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

Thread-static storage is per-thread storage of a static slot. On an instance field there is already one slot per object and the runtime ignores the attribute entirely, so the isolation the author asked for was never there. ⚠ The initializer case is worse than nothing and is the one people actually hit: the initializer runs in the static constructor, once, on whichever thread reaches the type first. That thread sees the value and every other thread sees default. Nothing throws, nothing warns, and the field reads correctly in the debugger on the thread that happens to be attached — which is why the bug survives review and is found from a null reference on a background thread three weeks later.

Example

Instead of:

sealed class Scratch {
    [ThreadStatic] StringBuilder buffer;              // not static: the attribute does nothing
    [ThreadStatic] static StringBuilder shared = new(); // only thread one sees the builder
}

Write:

sealed class Scratch {
    [ThreadStatic] static StringBuilder? buffer;

    static StringBuilder Buffer => buffer ??= new StringBuilder();
}

When it does not fire

The attribute must resolve to System.ThreadStaticAttribute by namespace-qualified name, so a same-named attribute of the author's own is never touched. ⚠ A `const` is excluded: it is implicitly static and is required to carry an initializer, so neither half of the rule can be true of it and the repair the second half offers would not compile. ⚠ `= 0`, `= false`, `= null` and `= default` are excluded, and that is not tidiness — those initializers assign exactly what every thread but the first already sees, so there is no divergence between threads to report, and firing on them would make the rule fire on a declaration that is merely verbose. An instance field carrying an initializer is reported once, as an instance field: the initializer is beside the point when the attribute is inert to begin with, and two findings on one declaration would be the same defect counted twice. The non-static half reports once for the declaration because the modifier is shared by every declarator; the initializer half reports once per declarator, because [ThreadStatic] static int a = 1, b; is wrong about a and right about b. ⚠ The fix for the non-static half deletes the attribute rather than inserting `static`, and the harness is what settled that. Adding static turns an instance field with an initializer into a static field with an initializer, which is the other half of this same rule — so the fix fired the rule again on its own output and skala fix would have looped. Deleting the annotation makes the declaration say what it already does, in one edit, from any starting shape; the other repair moves where the value lives and which threads share it, which is why neither fix is marked safe. Generated code is excluded.
